title: The 1966 George Wein jazz festival tour and the stage names
summary: In 1966 the tap dancers toured Europe with George Wein's festival, hoping to surprise Chuckles; their stage names were Kind Sir, Good Father, Tap Dancer's Dream and Godfather.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: No, no, no. No. In the Bert Wheeler Theater it started at like -- we come back in -- from -- 1966

we came back from a tour with a jazz festival, which was the George Wein, you know. He had a monarchy with the jazz musicians. And he was going to get -- you see, Chuckles was working for this Gezler Gunther over there. See, I think he was working in Paris at that time.

Now, George's a conception -- I mean consideration, I'll say. He wanted to surprise Chuckles, you know, and the other tap dancers, you see, which was -- because Chuckles, he was like a big brother to them, you see. So, I don't want to be, you know, fraudulent. I'll say it again, see, because it was a -- would have been a nice thing to happen, you know. I mean the reunion of two partners, you know, that had -- was on the top and they was getting ready to -- see, reinstate themselves, you see, but in another degree, see.

So, we got back in '66. And that's when this -- just before the Olympics started, you know. And they happen every four years, you see. And while we were over there with George Wein and the jazz festival, we were such an immediate success -- the tap dancers, see. First he was calling us just by individuality, like, you know, as they came on stage. Like Kind Sir, he came out first. That was Buster Brown. Then the Good Father, he came out second. That was Boston Jimmy Sly. Then the Tap Dancers Dream, Bravery -- that was Baby Lawrence, he came out. And then the Godfather was Chuck Green, and I came out fourth over there, okay.
But that was only stage names, you know. We was just saying that amongst ourselves as we were doing the tap dancing, the routines, see.
